locator: preamble, 'Still, moral realists are cognitivists insofar as they think moral statements are apt for robust truth and falsity and that many of them are in fact true.'
interpretation: The entry's characterization of moral realism, the reference theory of the deviation map. Read as: moral sentences are robustly truth-apt. That many are true is not formalized. Catholic natural law is realist in this sense (ST I-II q.94 a.4: practical truth the same for all). Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
